syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Let's Begin: recalling Lencho's story

concepts.learning_objective: Arrange the main events of 'A Letter to God' in their correct order.
Evaluate Lencho's faith in God and the irony of his attitude towards the post office employees.

topics.title: Reading Comprehension: The Trader and the Tailor

concepts.learning_objective: Recall and interpret the events of Rumi's story 'The Trader and the Tailor'.
Analyse the lesson of the story about pride, flattery and distraction.
Infer the meaning of words such as 'cordiality' from their use in the story.

topics.title: Vocabulary: 'light' compounds and word forms

concepts.learning_objective: Use compounds such as light-fingered, light year, light-headed and light-hearted correctly in context.
Identify how the same word works as different parts of speech, as in 'wound' and 'notice'.

topics.title: Grammar: relative clauses

concepts.learning_objective: Choose the correct relative pronoun (who, which, whom, whose) for a person or a thing.
Identify, form and punctuate relative clauses to combine and complete sentences.

topics.title: Editing: Lencho's thank-you letter

concepts.learning_objective: Supply the missing word in each line of a letter so that it is grammatically correct and complete.
Recognise common proofreading marks that editors use to correct writing.

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: The Race and man versus nature

concepts.learning_objective: Recall and interpret the events of the listening story 'The Race'.
Identify man versus nature as the conflict in Lencho's story.
Interpret the ideas of Norman Littleford's poem 'Man vs Nature'.

topics.title: Writing: character sketches and portraits

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the actions and qualities of Lencho and the tailor to write character sketches.
Select suitable details and adjectives to write a portrait of a person.

topics.title: The process approach to writing and project work

concepts.learning_objective: State the stages of the process approach to writing and what each stage focuses on.
Distinguish good practices of collaborative project work in the language classroom.

chapters.title: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom

topics.title: Reading: Sardar Patel's convocation speech on hard-won freedom
topics.ncert_sections: Let's Begin; Reading Comprehension, Text I (paragraphs 1-3)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the occasion of Sardar Patel's speech and the ideas he places before the graduates.
Explain why Patel says that freedom, once won, still has to be consolidated with responsibility.

topics.title: Reading: character, unity and the duty of the citizens of tomorrow

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Patel calls character the most essential requisite of university education.
Interpret Patel's warning about disunity and his call to the young to work for a strong, united nation.

topics.title: Vocabulary: words and idioms from the speech
topics.ncert_sections: Look Up and Understand; Vocabulary; Fun Facts (Idiom)

concepts.learning_objective: Infer and use the meanings of words such as conferring, precincts, unassailable and resurgence.
Use the idiom 'break the ice' and similar phrases appropriately in context.

topics.title: Grammar: use of articles

concepts.learning_objective: Use 'the' for specific or already-mentioned nouns, including nouns made specific by a phrase or clause.
Choose between 'a' and 'an' by the sound that follows and use them for non-specific nouns.

topics.title: Editing: finding and correcting errors in a passage

concepts.learning_objective: Correct errors in which the verb does not agree with its subject in number.
Correct errors in verb forms, tense and noun number in a passage.

topics.title: Let's Begin: revisiting 'His First Flight'

concepts.learning_objective: Recall why the young seagull feared flying and how hunger finally made him fly.
Explain how the seagull's family taunted and then tempted him into his first flight.

topics.title: Reading: 'All about a Dog' - the quarrel on the bus

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the sequence of events in the quarrel between the conductor and the passengers.
Interpret the narrator's portrait of the conductor as a 'Resentful Employee'.

topics.title: Reading: rules in the letter and in the spirit

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish rules that are hard and fast from rules meant for guidance and applied in their spirit.
Evaluate the narrator's advice to the conductor and how the story ends.

topics.title: Vocabulary: adverbs, prefixes and word meanings

concepts.learning_objective: Form adverbs from adjectives and verbs with correct spelling.
Form antonyms with the prefixes im-, il- and in-.
Infer the meanings of words such as imperturbably and indignant from the story.

topics.title: Grammar: phrasal verbs and the passive

concepts.learning_objective: Identify and use phrasal verbs with walk, take, give and put.
Change sentences into the passive in the required tense, with or without by + agent.

topics.title: Sentence building and editing

concepts.learning_objective: Unscramble jumbled words into meaningful, correctly ordered sentences.
Use capital letters, commas and full stops correctly when editing a passage.
Choose correctly among for, since and during.

topics.title: Listening and writing: riddles and rules in true spirit

concepts.learning_objective: Solve river-crossing riddles by reasoning aloud step by step.
Select ideas that show rules followed in the spirit for an article.

chapters.title: From the Diary of Anne Frank

topics.title: Text I: Nowrosji Kapadia and the Parsis of Delhi

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Nowrosji Kapadia's welcome at the railway station began the Parsi community in Delhi.
Infer the meaning of words such as cajole and overruled from their context in Text I.

topics.title: Text I: Parsi festive food and teatime traditions
topics.ncert_sections: Reading Comprehension, Text I (food and teatime)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the Parsi dishes described in the passage and what each one is.
Interpret what the community's festive cooking reveals about its values.
Analyse the writer's nostalgic memories of her grandmother and of teatime.

topics.title: Text II: Coffee from Araku Valley

concepts.learning_objective: Recall where Araku Valley is and how coffee came to it.
Explain how bio-dynamic farming and Adivasi ownership shape Araku coffee.
Identify words from Text II that match given meanings.

topics.title: Vocabulary and Grammar: sound words and participial adjectives

concepts.learning_objective: Match sound words such as clanking and rustling with their sources.
Use -ing and -ed participial adjectives correctly in sentences.
Rewrite present-tense sentences from the Coorg extract in the past tense.

topics.title: Editing: The Valley of Flowers

concepts.learning_objective: Correct misspelt words in the paragraph on the Valley of Flowers.
Distinguish commonly confused words such as advice and advise.
Explain why trekking and grazing were banned in the Valley of Flowers.

topics.title: Listening, Writing and Project: the Goan baker, Kashmiri breads and the Frontier Mail

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the main ideas of the listening passage on the Goan baker.
Recall the Kashmiri breads and the role of the Kandur shop.
Recall the key facts about the Frontier Mail given in the project.

topics.title: Mijbil and the author's care for him

concepts.learning_objective: Recall where otters like Mijbil come from and the setting of the author's home.
Identify the arrangements and care the author provided for his pet otter.
Link Mijbil's actions to the emotions they show.

topics.title: Reading Text I: Baby Bhakat, the civet cat

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the features and habits of the civet cat described in the passage.
Recall details of Bhakat's rescue, home and human family.
Infer how a wild animal helps maintain the balance of life in nature.

topics.title: Reading Text II: Human-wildlife conflict

concepts.learning_objective: State why humans and wildlife increasingly come into conflict.
Describe the impact of the conflict on people and animals.
Evaluate simple solutions that lead to mutually beneficial coexistence.

topics.title: Reading Text II: Animal rights

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what it means that animals have an inherent worth and can feel.
Distinguish equal consideration from equal treatment of animals.
Interpret how everyday choices can work as non-violent protest.

topics.title: Vocabulary: synonyms and words used as nouns and verbs

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the word that is not a synonym in a group of words.
Distinguish the use of the same word as a noun and as a verb.

topics.title: Grammar: noun modifiers, -ed/-ing adjectives, would and used to

concepts.learning_objective: Combine sentences using adjectives and adjective phrases as noun modifiers.
Choose correctly between -ed and -ing forms of adjectives.
Use 'would' and 'used to' correctly for repeated past actions and past states.

topics.title: Editing: punctuation and sentence reordering

concepts.learning_objective: Apply capital letters, commas, full stops and inverted commas correctly.
Rearrange jumbled parts into a meaningful, punctuated sentence.

topics.title: Listening: Gangaram, the friendly crocodile

concepts.learning_objective: Recall factual details from the listening text about Gangaram.
Interpret the story as an example of humans and animals living together.

topics.title: Valli's bus journey and the way characters speak

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the main events of Valli's bus ride to town and back, and how her feelings changed.
Explain how adverbs such as 'commandingly' and 'haughtily' reveal a speaker's mood and intention.

topics.title: Reading: Pedalling through the Golden Years

concepts.learning_objective: Understand the retired couple's cycling adventure in Uttarakhand and the reasons behind it.
Infer the meaning of words such as 'acclimatised' and 'encapsulates' from their context.

topics.title: Poem: Going Down Hill on a Bicycle, A Boy's Song

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the joy of the downhill ride and the message of the poem's closing lines.
Identify the comparisons and the address to the bird used in the poem.

topics.title: Vocabulary and grammar: phrasal verbs and confusable words

concepts.learning_objective: Identify phrasal verbs and complete sentences with the correct verb-particle combination.
Distinguish 'allusion' from 'illusion' and use the idiom 'turn a blind eye' correctly.

topics.title: Editing: the Sundarbans paragraph

concepts.learning_objective: Apply capital letters and full stops correctly to proper nouns and run-on sentences.
Correct misspelt words in a descriptive paragraph.

topics.title: Listening: Mizoram and its people

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the meaning of the name Mizoram and the features of its land.
Understand the link between Mizo festivals, farming and community dances.

topics.title: Speaking: offering help, asking for information and question tags
topics.ncert_sections: Speaking 2, Communicative Tasks I and II

concepts.learning_objective: Use polite expressions to offer, accept and refuse help.
Form correct question tags and recognise polite indirect requests for information.

topics.title: Let's Begin: 'Sermon' and 'Death Is Nothing At All'

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the religious or moral sense of 'sermon' from its sense of a long, tiresome lecture.
Interpret the consoling view of death in Canon Henry Scott Holland's 'Death Is Nothing At All' and compare it with the Buddha's sermon.

topics.title: Reading Comprehension: The Transformed Mind

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the Dalai Lama's view that the ultimate cause of human problems lies within the human mind.
Explain what the Dalai Lama means by spiritual development and what a compassionate heart brings.

topics.title: Reading Comprehension: The Ballad of Father Gilligan

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the events of the ballad and explain the old priest's feelings and actions.
Interpret the vocabulary and images of the ballad, such as 'flock' and the 'moth-hour'.
Analyse how the ballad shows God's care for a humble, tired servant.

topics.title: Vocabulary: Antonyms, Synonyms and Word Facts

concepts.learning_objective: Find antonyms of given words in the text of 'The Sermon at Benaras'.
Choose words nearest in meaning to words such as vow, preach, preserve, awaken and reign.
Recognise the silent 'w' and distinguish commonly confused words such as allude and elude.

topics.title: Grammar: Reported Speech

concepts.learning_objective: Change statements and questions from direct to reported speech with correct changes of person, tense and reporting verb.
Report requests and commands using verbs such as told and asked with a to-infinitive.

topics.title: Editing: The Wild Geese

concepts.learning_objective: Supply missing prepositions in a narrative paragraph.
Supply missing articles, conjunctions and pronouns so that a paragraph reads correctly.

topics.title: Listening: The Sanchi Stupa

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the location, period, builder and later additions of the Sanchi Stupa.
Explain how the gateways of the Sanchi Stupa depict the Buddha's life symbolically.

topics.title: The story of the play: the proposal and the two quarrels

concepts.learning_objective: Recall why Lomov visits Chubukov and how his proposal keeps getting delayed.
Explain how the dispute over the Oxen Meadows interrupts the proposal.
Interpret the second quarrel, over the dogs Guess and Squeezer, and the way the play ends.

topics.title: The characters: Lomov, Natalya and Chubukov

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Lomov as a nervous, complaining hypochondriac who decides to marry for practical reasons.
Describe Natalya as a strong-willed, quarrelsome young woman who cares about her family's property.
Analyse Chubukov's changing attitude towards Lomov and the self-interest behind it.

topics.title: Theme and form: satire, farce and irony

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the play satirises the landowning class that treats marriage as a matter of property.
Identify the play as a one-act farce and interpret its irony, especially in its ending.

topics.title: Words and expressions from the play

concepts.learning_objective: Work out the meanings of words such as 'palpitations', 'impudence' and 'overshot' as used in the play.
Interpret how the characters' ways of speaking create humour and move the plot.

topics.title: Grammar: reporting the dialogue of the play

concepts.learning_objective: Change statements, questions and commands from the play's dialogue into reported speech.
Identify declarative, interrogative, imperative and exclamatory sentences in dramatic dialogue.
